- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.4) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns positive after a dip.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp price spikes, leading to premature downward corrections.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising, then underestimate later days when sentiment stabilizes or declines.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — model often assumes trend continuation when sentiment is mixed or turning.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to overfit recent momentum — reduce forecast slope for sustained high sentiment.
